pass_a_gloss: [fragment opens mid-word] but new heavens and a new earth and his promises we await, according to what is written. And the Savior himself said something such: 'In those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.' For the glory itself of the Savior will suffice for the saints for illumination. But so that the things set forth may seem somehow to follow the sense of the [verses] above, having praised this interpretation, we say also something other is signified through the set-forth lines. For the sun's light, and besides the moon's, is useful and necessary to the eyes of the body. But at night the sun's light is drawn in, and by day that of the moon; for alternately they yield the shining to one another. But the divine and intelligible [light], which the Savior of all sends into the hearts of those who have believed, he says, through the Holy Spirit, and through those who know well how to initiate into mysteries, will be unquenchable and unceasing and ever-shining, so that the mind of each stands in need neither of sun nor of moon for illumination or recovery of sight; for the mind is not lit by perceptible light, but is rather content with the light-guidance through the Holy Spirit, and with brightness, toward being able to behold the glory of Christ, and how much likeness he would have toward the one who begot him, essentially of course, yes indeed also unerringly to know the way of the best life. Therefore the Savior has become everlasting light for us, and makes this plain to us, saying: 'I am the light of the world,' and again: 'Whenever I am in the world, I am light of the world.' 'The one following me will surely not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.' [Lemma, Isaiah 60:20b–22:] And the days of your mourning will be filled up, and your people all righteous, and through the age they will inherit the land, guarding the planting, works of his hands, for glory. The fewest will be for thousands, and the least for a great nation. I, the Lord, according to seasons will gather them. Those who say the time of the consummation is made plain through the sun's or moon's light no longer operating, but rather being drawn in, so that our Lord may become everlasting light, say that to those mourning now, whom indeed the Savior says will be comforted, there will be an end of mourning [source breaks off mid-word].

lemmas.gloss: to lead into the mysteries, initiate

pass_b_english: … but we await new heavens and a new earth, and his promises, as it is written (2 Peter 3:13). The Savior himself said something of the same kind: “In those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light” (Mark 13:24; compare Matthew 24:29). For the glory of the Savior itself will be enough to give the saints their light.

But so that the present words may seem in some way to follow the sense of the verses before them, we approve this interpretation and say that the present lines also signify something else. The light of the sun, and that of the moon as well, is useful and necessary to the eyes of the body. Yet at night the sun’s light is withdrawn, and by day the moon’s, for they take turns yielding the work of shining to each other.

But the divine and spiritual light, he says, which the Savior of all puts into the hearts of believers through the Holy Spirit and through those who know well how to lead others into the mysteries, will be unquenchable, unceasing, and always shining. So the mind of each person stands in need neither of sun nor of moon to be enlightened or to see. For the mind is not lit by light that the senses perceive. It is content instead with the guiding light that comes through the Holy Spirit, and with a brightness that lets it behold the glory of Christ and how great a likeness he bears to the One who begot him, a likeness of essence, of course, and also lets it know without straying the way of the best life.

The Savior, then, has become everlasting light for us, and he makes this plain to us when he says, “I am the light of the world” (John 8:12), and again, “As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world” (John 9:5), and, “Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life” (John 8:12).

“And the days of your mourning will be fulfilled, and your people will all be righteous, and they will inherit the land forever, guarding the planting, the works of his hands, for glory. The fewest will become thousands, and the least a great nation. I, the Lord, will gather them in due season” (Isaiah 60:20–22).

Those who say that the time of the consummation is indicated by the light of the sun or the moon no longer working, but rather being withdrawn so that our Lord may become everlasting light, say that for those who mourn now, whom the Savior also says will be comforted (Matthew 5:4), there will be an end of mourning …

choices.why: Set against αἰσθητῷ φωτί (light perceived by the senses) a few lines later; the light is known by the mind, given through the Holy Spirit.
Names the teachers who initiate believers; 'mystagogy' would be a transliteration.

choices.english: a likeness of essence, of course
choices.why: Qualifies the Son's ἐμφέρεια to the Father who begot him; the doctrinal point is that the likeness is in essence, not mere resemblance, so it is kept explicit.
Paired with φωτισμόν as what the mind needs light for; 'recovery of sight' would import a healing image the sentence does not develop.

choices.english: the sense of the verses before them
choices.why: ἀνόπιν means 'above, earlier'; Cyril approves the literal end-time reading and then offers a second, spiritual one that fits the preceding verses.

bible_refs.note: καινοὺς δὲ οὐρανοὺς καὶ καινὴν γῆν … προσδοκῶμεν matches 2 Peter 3:13; Cyril has the plural τὰ ἐπαγγέλματα and adds κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον.
Ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ὁ ἥλιος σκοτισθήσεται, καὶ ἡ σελήνη οὐ δώσει τὸ φέγγος αὐτῆς: 'in those days' is Mark 13:24; Matthew 24:29 has the same sun and moon clauses.

Ἐγώ εἰμι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου and Ὁ ἀκολουθῶν ἐμοὶ, οὐ μὴ περιπατήσῃ ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ, ἀλλ' ἕξει τὸ φῶς τῆς ζωῆς are both John 8:12; Cyril quotes the two halves either side of John 9:5, so the citation appears twice inline.
Ὅταν ὦ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, φῶς εἰμι τοῦ κόσμου = John 9:5, word order slightly varied.
Lemma set off by the source's 9…9 markers: the last clause of LXX Isaiah 60:20 (days of mourning fulfilled), 60:21 and 60:22. Isaiah verse numbers are the same in the LXX and the Hebrew here.
τοῖς πενθοῦσι … οὓς δὴ καὶ παρακληθήσεσθαί φησιν ὁ Σωτὴρ echoes μακάριοι οἱ πενθοῦντες, ὅτι αὐτοὶ παρακληθήσονται (Matthew 5:4).

source_normalizations: 2026-10-23: the locked row was in the PDF's Latin-letter Greek font encoding (backslash and slash accents, j for final sigma). It was decoded character by character to Unicode polytonic Greek; spacing, line breaks, hyphen breaks, the 6/9 quotation and lemma markers and the column numbers 70.1348 and 481 are kept as printed. No letters were added or changed.
reviewer: claude-review:waveA-20261023 rv10 (clause-by-clause check against the decoded Greek)
review_notes: Every clause checked against the decoded Greek: no omissions or additions; negation (οὐ δώσει, οὐ μὴ περιπατήσῃ, μήτε … μήτε), agency and modality kept.
Fix made before assembly: 'no longer stands in need of sun or moon' added 'no longer' to ὥστε μήτε ἡλίου μήτε σελήνης ἐν χρείᾳ καθεστηκέναι; now 'stands in need neither of sun nor of moon'.
The block opens mid-word ('ης,') and ends mid-word ('κατ…'); both breaks are marked with an ellipsis and nothing is filled in.
The closing sentence reports other interpreters (Οἱ … λέγοντες … φασίν) and is kept as their view, not Cyril's.
Scripture checked: 2 Peter 3:13, Mark 13:24 with Matthew 24:29, John 8:12, John 9:5, Isaiah 60:20–22, Matthew 5:4.
